papers.title: The Ramification Index: Original composite
papers.thesis: Original composite DRAM-price index establishing a 6/6 recession signal across 40 years and Granger causality to GDP.
papers.abstract: The original Ramification Index: a single composite DRAM-price indicator covering 1980–2023. Established the 6/6 NBER recession signal and the first Granger-causality test from DRAM prices to real GDP growth. Superseded by v2 (bifurcation) and v3 (self-audit of data provenance and statistical power).

papers.title: The Ramification Index v2: The Bifurcated Index
papers.thesis: Splits the index into commodity DRAM (R_C) and AI/HBM (R_AI) sub-indices; documents RAMageddon 2026 and Granger causality to GDP.
papers.abstract: A supply-side macroeconomic indicator built on DRAM prices. v2 introduces bifurcated sub-indices separating commodity DRAM from AI/HBM markets, documents the 2025–2026 RAMageddon event, and demonstrates Granger causality from the RAM index to real GDP growth. 6 of 6 NBER recessions covered; correlation r = 0.41 with real GDP YoY.
papers.cite: Wakil, K. (2025). The Ramification Index v2: The Bifurcated Index. Knowware Institute. ram-index.com

papers.title: v3: Provenance, Construction, and What the Series Can Support
papers.thesis: Correction, not a new result: source recovered, 1988 endpoint restored, Granger result restated as untested pending higher-frequency data.
papers.byline: Khayyam Wakil · Aug 2026 · corrected dataset + 8-guard protocol
papers.abstract: This third version is a correction and a method, not a new result. (1) The primary source for the 1980–2017 segment — the McCallum memory-price archive — has lapsed; the original workbook is recovered from the Internet Archive and republished. (2) The 1988 "RAM drought" is absent from the published price table; the recovered archive shows a +82.5% move where the published series shows −21.8%. (3) A point-in-time construction standard is specified, with a monthly index (RI-M) built from the recovered archive. (4) The v2 Granger result is carried by its last six observations; withholding 2020–2026 flips the forward p-value from 0.0243 to 0.2984. A corrected quality-adjusted series is published alongside the original — nothing is overwritten — with an eight-guard test protocol.
papers.cite: Wakil, K. (2026). The Ramification Index v3: Provenance, Construction, and What the Series Can Support. Knowware Institute. ram-index.com/v3

papers.title: v3: The Bifurcated Index, Granger Causality, Supply-Side Divergence, and the Practitioner Gap
papers.thesis: Extends v2 in eight ways — bifurcation, Granger causality, RAMageddon 2025–2026, oligopoly cartel history, and the practitioner gap.
papers.byline: Khayyam Wakil · Aug 2026 · 46 years of data (1980–2026)
papers.abstract: The Ramification Index names the DRAM commodity, the economic ramifications of oligopoly pricing decisions, and the algebraic ramification index of a prime ideal — all three describe how a DRAM price movement propagates outward into server capex, AI infrastructure, consumer electronics, and macro activity. This third version extends the original in eight ways: (1) bifurcates the index into Commodity and AI sub-indices; (2) presents Granger tests showing the index leads real GDP at 1–3 quarter lags (F = 5.83, p = 0.004); (3) documents the 2025–2026 RAMageddon — the sharpest positive reading in the index's 46-year history; (4) integrates DRAM price-fixing conviction history (1998–2006); and names the practitioner gap between folk indicators and formal signals.
papers.cite: Wakil, K. (2026). The Ramification Index v3: The Bifurcated Index, Granger Causality, Supply-Side Divergence, and the Practitioner Gap. Knowware Institute (arXiv preprint). ram-index.com

papers.title: v4: A Fourth Firm, and Why It Fails the Scope Condition
papers.thesis: CXMT's state-administered price does not extend the index — it tightens the scope condition. The fourth firm is untestable, not a fifth regime.
papers.byline: Khayyam Wakil · Aug 2026 · continuation of the audit line
papers.abstract: This fourth version continues the audit line of v3 (Provenance). It asks a single question: does the July 2026 public listing of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) — the first credible fourth DRAM entrant — change what the series can support? It concludes it does not. (1) CXMT's price is policy-administered: state mandate, export-control isolation, blacklisted buyer set, and an equity that opened +466% pricing a geopolitical option. By v3's scope condition it lacks a fast, elastic, private-market price and belongs with potash — untestable — not with incumbent DRAM. (2) The nearest precedent, 1988, is also missing from the series; both episodes are trade-policy-driven. (3) A fourth firm optimising for self-sufficiency is a mid-sample break; it makes the n = 46 panel less poolable, not more. (4) The China/RoW split is populated for zero realised observations and logged as a watch-item. The earlier draft's "fifth regime" claim is withdrawn as premature.
papers.cite: Wakil, K. (2026). The Ramification Index v4: A Fourth Firm, and Why It Fails the Scope Condition. Knowware Institute. ram-index.com

papers.title: v4: The Contested Oligopoly — CXMT, the Fourth Firm, and the Geopolitical Ramification of Memory
papers.thesis: A fourth, state-backed entrant breaks the oligopoly coordination assumption and introduces a geographic bifurcation and a false-positive subsidy regime.
papers.byline: Khayyam Wakil · Aug 2026 · extension to v3 (Practitioner Gap line)
papers.abstract: This fourth version extends v3 in four ways, all organised around the July 2026 CXMT listing. (1) Documents the entry of a fourth manufacturer holding ~7.7–9% of global DRAM and its record STAR Market debut; shows why a state-backed firm optimising for self-sufficiency rather than oligopoly pricing discipline breaks the coordination assumption. (2) Introduces a second bifurcation — geographic — because U.S. export controls firewall China-domestic DRAM from the rest of the world. (3) Adds a fifth interpretive regime (subsidised-supply divergence), observationally the mirror of a recession signal, creating a false-positive risk the index must guard against. (4) Specifies how to admit CXMT without importing the 466% policy premium embedded in its equity. The fourth firm does not dissolve the oligopoly; it makes the oligopoly contested, and a contested oligopoly ramifies differently.
papers.cite: Wakil, K. (2026). The Ramification Index v4: The Contested Oligopoly — CXMT, the Fourth Firm, and the Geopolitical Ramification of Memory. Knowware Institute. ram-index.com

NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee official start/end dates; 6 cycles covered (1980, 1981, 1990, 2001, 2007, 2020).
SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron quarterly earnings; IDC server DRAM shipment data; Omdia HBM revenue estimates.
Yahoo Finance via yfinance; 11-stock panel: MU, 005930.KS, 000660.KS, 688825.SS, NVDA, TSM, AMD, INTC, QCOM, WDC, STX.
ChangXin Memory Technologies S-1, STAR Market listing (July 2026); IDC/Omdia DRAM share estimates; U.S. BIS export-control action list.
